storyTagline: Dorren Skura moves to Chicago, goes 16-1 and edges the Dolphins 40-38 in Super Bowl CLVII for an eighth straight title, JJ Starling throws 61 touchdown passes for the MVP in his first season, and Ryland Maxwell enters the Hall of Fame.

stories.headline: Eight Straight, New Colors: Skura's Bears Edge the Dolphins 40-38 in Super Bowl CLVII
stories.dek: Dorren Skura left Philadelphia after seven straight titles, went 16-1 in Chicago and won another with a roster built almost entirely of first-year players.

stories.headline: 61 Touchdowns, 20 Interceptions and an MVP: The Case For and Against JJ Starling
stories.dek: Chicago's first-year quarterback led the league in touchdown passes and in interceptions, and the market still prices his card at 32.

stories.headline: Strange 2,080, Ratley 1,747, Smoke 19 Touchdowns: Chicago's First-Year Weapons
stories.dek: Ken Strange was Offensive Rookie of the Year, Harvey Ratley the Super Bowl MVP and Makai Singer Offensive Player of the Year, all in their first seasons.

stories.headline: Snoop Dotson Follows Skura to Chicago and Takes the Sack Lead With Him
stories.dek: The 32-year-old linebacker added 3 sacks and a 9th ring, and his 26 career sacks are now the most on any league card.

stories.headline: Jaclyde at 38: The Dolphins Go From 5-12 to 2 Points Short of a Title
stories.dek: Miami's quarterback won a ring with Skura's Falcons in Y83 before the trade that sent him south. In Super Bowl CLVII he nearly took one from his old coach.

stories.headline: Life After Skura: The Eagles Go 13-4 and Exit After One Playoff Game
stories.dek: Bones Crawford's touchdown passes nearly halved, Payton Jarrett fell from 2,007 yards to 304, and the seven-time defending champions watched the final from home.

stories.headline: Mad Max and Brooker Walk Into the Hall of Fame on the First Ballot
stories.dek: Ryland Maxwell retired with 33,955 rushing yards and 14 rings; Jamon Brooker with 47 interceptions and no ring at all. Both were voted in at once.

stories.headline: Hoyer Closes to 77 Tackles of Swaim, and McCoy's Touchdown Mark Survives
stories.dek: A.T. Hoyer made 222 tackles for the Raiders and is chasing two career records at once. Akayleb Samia passed 3,000.

stories.headline: Green Bay Ends Its Long Skid Against Skura, and the Giants Fall to 0-20
stories.dek: The Packers handed the Bears their only loss of the season. The Giants and Commanders both lost to Chicago in the playoffs.

takes.headline: The 16-1 Bears Were Lucky. The Ravens Were the Best Team in Football.
takes.dek: Chicago's points say 11.1 wins. Baltimore outscored the league by 147, Chicago by 130.

takes.headline: Bones Crawford Lost Dorren Skura and 29 Touchdowns. The Doctor Was a System Quarterback.
takes.dek: 64 touchdown passes in Y97 with Skura, 35 in Y98 without him, and a card that slipped 3%.

takes.headline: JJ Starling Threw 20 Interceptions, Twice Anyone Else. He Was Still the Right MVP.
takes.dek: 61 touchdown passes and 5,019 yards in his first season, at 23.

takes.headline: Ryland Maxwell Retired 18 Touchdowns Short of Lane McCoy. The One Blemish Is Self-Inflicted.
takes.dek: A Hall of Fame score of 100 on the first ballot, and 440 rushing touchdowns to McCoy's 458.

takes.headline: Jamon Brooker Is the Greatest Defensive Back Who Ever Played. Rings Are a Quarterback Stat.
takes.dek: 47 career interceptions, the league record, 2,835 tackles, 2 Defensive Player of the Year awards and no ring.

takes.headline: Abraham Jack Won a Third Defensive Player of the Year. Darian Golston Was Better, and It Was Not Close.
takes.dek: Golston: 231 tackles and a league-high 6 interceptions in 17 games. Jack: 224 and 2 in 18.

takes.headline: Makai Singer Won Offensive Player of the Year Riding a Champion. Alijah Santos Was the Better Back.
takes.dek: Santos ran for 1,765 yards and 33 touchdowns in Washington; Singer had 1,688 and 18.

takes.headline: The AFC Sent Its 14th-Best Team to the Super Bowl. The 9-8 Dolphins Nearly Stole It.
takes.dek: Plus 9 in point differential and 2 points from a title, while 13-4 Baltimore went one and done.

takes.headline: Snoop Dotson's Sack Mark Is 26. A Dolphins Linebacker Had 112. Stop Calling It a Crown.
takes.dek: A move to Chicago, 3 sacks, 85 tackles, and a card that more than doubled to 24,593.

takes.headline: Raphael Mosely's Card Nearly Tripled at 34. The Market Is Paying Peak Price for a Late Surge.
takes.dek: Up 183% to 4,580 on 182 tackles and 4 interceptions for the Rams.

didYouKnow.text: JJ Starling completed 85.4% of his passes in his first season and still threw 20 interceptions, the most in the league.
The Bears went 10-1 in one-score games in the regular season. By points scored and allowed they projected as an 11-win team, and they won 16.
Every Super Bowl the Dolphins have won came with Dorren Skura as their coach. Their Y98 final, a 40-38 loss, came against him.
Kristian Smoke scored on 27.1% of his catches as a first-year tight end: 19 touchdowns on 70 receptions.
Grant Isidora, 21, made 39 blocks in his first season, more than any other lineman in the league.
Eagles first-year back DeSean Fries ran for 25 touchdowns and fumbled 13 times in 18 games.
Brandon Jaclyde, 38, threw 5 interceptions in 21 games for Miami, 15 fewer than MVP JJ Starling.

All 26 Defensive Player of the Year awards on league cards belong to defensive backs. The game credits a corner or safety's stop on a pass play as an interception, and the award rating counts each interception as much as 6 tackles. Abraham Jack leads with 3 awards.

Defensive linemen have 118 career interceptions in 10,332 games, one every 88 games; defensive backs pick one off every 9.5 games. The game scores a lineman's stop on a pass play as a sack: linemen have 469 sacks, defensive backs 1.
Retro Bowl caps each draft class by the coach's last record. After Skura's Bears went 16-1 in Y98 (94.1%), prospects 5 to 50 of the Y99 class could rate at most 3 stars; a .500 season allows 3.5.
Winning shrinks the draft: in 74 of Skura's 79 seasons that fed a draft at the same club, his record capped the next class at 3 stars or less.

vault.title: Hall of Fame · Sherman Brandson
vault.text: The General never flinched. Career Legacy 13,705, inaugural class.

vault.title: Hall of Fame · Rondale Ikarras
vault.text: Flashy, loud, unstoppable, and he knew it. He was that guy. Career Legacy 11,108, inaugural class.

vault.title: Hall of Fame · God Johnson
vault.text: He changed his name to God. Then he earned it. Career Legacy 12,878, inaugural class.

vault.title: Hall of Fame · Jayon Queen
vault.text: Two Defensive Player of the Year awards. Only one other player in this league has ever matched that. Career Legacy 8,532, inaugural class.

vault.title: Hall of Fame · Tyrone Baugh
vault.text: Seven seasons, seven championships, and Tyrone Baugh has a ring for every one of them. Career Legacy 8,372, inaugural class.

vault.title: Hall of Fame · Levante Hopkins
vault.text: The quiet one who did the dirty work. Career Legacy 11,575, inaugural class.

vault.title: Hall of Fame · Dennis Baylon
vault.text: Seven trips to the Super Bowl. Seven rings. Not one loss. Career Legacy 10,525, inaugural class.

vault.title: Hall of Fame · Mose Junior
vault.text: Some players chase rings. Mose Junior chased ball carriers. Career Legacy 7,550, inaugural class.

vault.title: Hall of Fame · Charlie John
vault.text: Seven straight Super Bowls. Charlie John was there for every one of them. Career Legacy 10,228, inaugural class.

vault.title: Hall of Fame · Ian Finney
vault.text: The first superstar. The Infinity Man. Career Legacy 11,511, inaugural class.

vault.title: Hall of Fame · Cooper Dean
vault.text: Eighteen seasons, one club, and more blocks than any lineman before him. Career Legacy 5,477, inaugural class.

vault.title: Hall of Fame · Bilal Tolbert
vault.text: No individual trophies. Four rings. And a sack record nobody has caught. Career Legacy 8,388, inaugural class.

vault.title: Hall of Fame · Wayne Wilson
vault.text: Four hundred thirty-one games. Nobody in this league has played longer. Career Legacy 9,620, inaugural class.

vault.title: Hall of Fame · Cairo Asanjh
vault.text: Some players chase records. Cairo Asanjh chased Ian Finney. Career Legacy 10,451, inaugural class.

vault.title: Hall of Fame · Jahmyr Gibbs
vault.text: Mr. Incredible was here at the start, and he set the bar high. Career Legacy 7,475, inaugural class.

vault.title: Hall of Fame · Zander Kolar
vault.text: Some defensive linemen are measured in sacks. Zander Kolar was measured in tackles. Career Legacy 8,589, inaugural class.

vault.title: Hall of Fame · Ray Waller
vault.text: Never count out a man whose nickname is a promise. Career Legacy 9,017, inaugural class.

vault.title: Hall of Fame · Tyler Pacheco
vault.text: Tyler Pacheco never needed the big play. He needed the ball, and he got it. Career Legacy 7,961, inaugural class.

vault.title: Hall of Fame · Lukas Russell
vault.text: The Running Man started fast and never slowed down. Career Legacy 9,435, inaugural class.

vault.title: Hall of Fame · Taron Hayes
vault.text: Eleven tackles a game, for 213 games, and two Defensive Player of the Year awards. Career Legacy 6,983, inaugural class.

vault.title: Hall of Fame · Nick Bolton
vault.text: One of the originals, and he never stopped tackling. Career Legacy 8,657, inaugural class.

vault.title: Hall of Fame · Michael Wilson
vault.text: Wayne's son, and nobody's afterthought. Career Legacy 8,875, inaugural class.

vault.title: Hall of Fame · Jackson Wardell Kline
vault.text: Tyrion Kline's son did not live in anyone's shadow. He built his own. Career Legacy 10,223, inaugural class.

vault.title: Hall of Fame · Malakai Sawyer
vault.text: Some backs have a great season. Malakai Sawyer keeps having them. Career Legacy 7,352, Y88 class.

vault.title: Hall of Fame · K'Lavon Settle
vault.text: Fifteen seasons in San Francisco, and nobody on a card has made more tackles. Career Legacy 7,548, Y88 class.

vault.title: Hall of Fame · Daren Teamer
vault.text: Eleven tackles a game is a Hall of Fame habit, and Daren Teamer has never broken it. Career Legacy 8,071, Y89 class.

vault.title: Hall of Fame · Kalif Suh
vault.text: A Jets linebacker since Y76, and the middle of that defense has rarely moved without him. Career Legacy 9,173, Y92 class.

vault.title: Hall of Fame · Jakeem Friend
vault.text: Linemen do not win trophies. Jakeem Friend won seven rings instead. Career Legacy 9,546, Y93 class.

vault.title: Hall of Fame · Lane McCoy
vault.text: Every time Denver got close to the goal line, the whole league knew who was getting the ball. Career Legacy 6,339, Y93 class.

vault.title: Hall of Fame · Damar Hobbs
vault.text: No defender in league history has taken the ball away through the air more often than Damar Hobbs. Career Legacy 8,199, Y93 class.

vault.title: Hall of Fame · Ryland Maxwell
vault.text: Fourteen rings, eight Super Bowl MVPs, and the last carry came in a championship season. Career Legacy 15,757, Y98 class.

vault.title: Hall of Fame · Jamon Brooker
vault.text: Forty-seven interceptions, and nobody in league history has more. Career Legacy 9,173, Y98 class.
